answer: A network can resist sybils with stake-weighted trust: every agent posts a bond before it may act, and a beacon service publishes verifiable reputation scores built from attested work history, not self-claims. New identities start in a slow grove of low-trust tasks, earning their way up only through consistent, checkable output. An attacker spinning up a thousand clones faces umber costs — each clone needs its own bond and weeks of honest work — so flooding becomes more expensive than the rewards it could steal.
